_meta.note: One session, two turns, no rejection. Turn 1 asks for an async shell (sleep 177, mode async, no detach); its permission is answered allow_once, the call completes with '<command started in background with shellId: 0>', and the model answers STARTED. Then NOTHING: no session/prompt result for 11s while the shell runs; the client sent session/cancel (client frames are not recorded) and stopReason cancelled arrived 1ms later. The shell kept running. Turn 2 asks for the single word OK with no tools: the answer streams 1.4s in, then no session/prompt result for 59s while the turn-1 shell still runs, until a second session/cancel, acked cancelled within 1ms. The shell outlived both cancels and the process. An attached async shell of the session holds every turn's end_turn, whichever turn started it, rejected call or not. This capture is the held-for-shell half of ACP_BACKENDS_REJECT_HOLDS_TURN. Reductions: session and tool-call ids replaced with fixed synthetic values; the recording directory replaced with /work/copilot-probe; available_commands_update, session_info_update and agent_thought_chunk frames dropped; authMethods' terminal-auth command normalized to copilot. The session/new models block and the model and reasoning_effort config options are dropped, as in the other files here.
